name: Bradley Mottier Innovation Challenge in Systems Engineering
description: A fall semester competition run by the Industrial and Enterprise Systems Engineering department where small teams develop an innovative idea through reports and a final presentation. Up to 10 teams are accepted, competing for cash prizes with expense reimbursement.
good_for: ISE students developing an innovation with prize money
parent_org: Department of Industrial and Enterprise Systems Engineering (ISE)
ideal_participant: Grainger Engineering teams of 2 to 4 with at least 2 ISE students
deadline_note: 2026 applications closed Sep 13, 2026. Remaining 2026 dates: final reports Nov 29, final presentation Dec 4, winners announced Dec 10 (per program page). Next application window expected Fall 2027.
cost_or_funding: Prizes of $5,000, $2,000, and $1,000, plus up to $500 expense reimbursement per team (per program page)
notes: Status evidence: Official page lists the 2026 timeline: application deadline Sep 13, final presentation Dec 4, winners announced Dec 10. No more than 3 graduate students per team. Contact is Julie Murphy, ISE Director of Alumni Relations. next_deadline is the 2026 final presentation, relevant only to accepted teams.

name: Cozad New Venture Challenge
description: UIUC's largest annual startup competition, where student teams get workshops, mentors, and a spring Demo Day and finals to compete for prizes and investment. No prototype is needed, and there are tracks such as Technology, Healthcare, and Consumer Packaged Goods.
good_for: Turning a startup idea into a funded venture
ideal_participant: Any UIUC student team with a startup idea
deadline_note: Landuyt events calendar shows Cozad Registration entries running Dec 1, 2026 through Feb 2, 2027; the exact 2027 registration deadline is not stated. 2026 cycle: registration closed Feb 1, 2026, Demo Day Apr 16, 2026, finals Apr 17, 2026.
cost_or_funding: Over $700,000 in prizes and investments awarded in 2026, including a $100,000 Grand Prize (per program page)
notes: Status evidence: Program page reports the 2026 competition (26th year) awarded over $700,000; schedule page lists 2026 finals on Apr 17, 2026; Landuyt calendar lists Cozad Registration entries from Dec 1, 2026 to Feb 2, 2027. Online track is limited to Gies iMBA and MCS Chicago students. Schedule page still shows the 2026 timeline.

name: Health Make-A-Thon
description: A Carle Illinois innovation competition where teams build prototypes for healthcare problems and pitch them to judges. The most recent edition was a two-day patient-centered event pairing CI MED students and collaborators with real patients, with prize money for top teams.
good_for: Prototyping a health solution in a short team competition
parent_org: Health Maker Lab, Carle Illinois College of Medicine
ideal_participant: Carle Illinois medical students and collaborators from design, engineering, and business
deadline_note: Most recent edition was a fall 2025 Patient-Centered Health Make-a-Thon (news dated Dec 11, 2025). No 2026 date posted.
cost_or_funding: 2025 edition had a $10,000 prize pool ($5,000, $3,000, $2,000 for top three) per the Dec 2025 Carle Illinois news story; 2026 prizes not posted.
notes: Format has changed over time. Early editions (2018 to 2020) were open to all Illinois residents with $10,000 in lab resources for each of 10 winners. The current events page describes a Fall Make-a-Thon for CI MED students that feeds into the Cozad New Venture Challenge health care track. 2025 teams included students from Art and Design, Gies, Grainger, and LAS. Updates sign-up form: https://forms.illinois.edu/sec/549661001.

name: EnterpriseWorks Incubator (and EW 2.0)
description: The startup incubator at the center of Research Park, offering offices, wet labs, entrepreneur-in-residence advising, and corporate connections to university and community startups. EW 2.0 is a planned growth-stage expansion building next door with lab, manufacturing, and office space for scaling companies.
good_for: Getting lab or office space and incubation for a tech startup
parent_org: Research Park / Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation
ideal_participant: University and community founders with a tech venture who need space and incubation
notes: Status evidence: EnterpriseWorks page shows Aug 2026 news (Cache Energy, ForgeBee 2026 Momentum Awards finalist); Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article describes EnterpriseWorks and plans for EW 2.0. EW 2.0 = 'EnterpriseWorks 2.0', a planned growth-stage incubator building adjacent to EnterpriseWorks, funded by state capital including a DCEO Tech Incubator Enhancement Grant and IFAB Tech Hub funding; as of Aug 21, 2026 still described as plans, no opening date. The /enterpriseworks footer link redirects to an unrelated news article (EnterpriseWorks awarded University Center grant), so use the locate-here page. Contact email is the general Research Park address.

name: EnterpriseWorks Incubator (labs, offices, and makerspace)
description: The Research Park's startup incubator offers wet labs, offices, and a shared makerspace with tools like a 3D printer, laser cutter, lathe, and mill, plus access to EnterpriseWorks programming.
good_for: Finding lab, office, and prototyping space for a tech startup
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: University-affiliated and community tech startups needing lab or office space
deadline_note: Tenancy inquiries accepted on a rolling basis.
notes: Status evidence: Incubator page shows 2026 news, including TIME/Statista recognition as one of America's Best Incubators & Accelerators 2026 and an Aug 21, 2026 graduate news item. Makerspace page (dated 2019) says it is free for Research Park companies, EnterpriseWorks tenants, and affiliate members; individual students without a resident company are not listed as eligible. Rent and tenancy criteria are not published.

name: I-Start Program
description: A first-year startup services program announced by EnterpriseWorks in 2011 that cost-shared help with business planning, legal setup, SBIR applications, accounting, marketing, and HR for new University of Illinois startups.
good_for: New university spinouts needing first-year business services
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: University of Illinois faculty or other entrepreneurs launching a company around a university technology
deadline_note: No application cycle found.
notes: Likely defunct: the only official source is a 2011 announcement of a DCEO-funded pilot (about 15 startups over 18 months). I-Start does not appear on the current Research Park resources page. Recommend removing or marking inactive unless EnterpriseWorks confirms it still runs.

name: iVenture Accelerator
description: A 10-week, full-time summer accelerator at Gies for student-led startups that want to scale. Teams get up to $20,000 in non-dilutive support (capacity funding plus stipends), mentorship, and go-to-market training, and no equity is taken.
good_for: Student founders ready to work full-time on a startup over the summer
parent_org: Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, Gies College of Business
ideal_participant: A University of Illinois student founder with up to 4 teammates (majority Illinois students holding majority ownership) who can commit 10 weeks full-time in summer
deadline_note: Summer 2026 cohort: Wave 1 closed Nov 3, 2025; Final Wave closed March 7, 2026, per the apply page. Rolling feedback offered. No summer 2027 deadline posted as of 2026-10-13.
cost_or_funding: Up to $20,000 non-dilutive ($10,000 capacity funding plus $2,500 stipends for up to 4 full-time team members); no equity taken (per iventure.illinois.edu). Non-Illinois team members do not receive stipends.
notes: Status evidence: Apply page lists a Final Wave deadline of Saturday, March 7, 2026 for the summer cohort (iventure.illinois.edu/apply). Site describes iVenture as the capstone of the 'Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship', suggesting OVAEL (Origin Ventures Academy for Entrepreneurial Leadership) has been renamed. Related credit courses: BADM 463/464 iVenture Accelerator Seminars.

name: AWARE (Accelerating Women and underRepresented Entrepreneurs)
description: An EnterpriseWorks program, first funded by an NSF grant, that gave women and underrepresented founders training, mentoring from an entrepreneur-in-residence, networking, and small proof-of-concept grants for teams.
good_for: Women and underrepresented founders seeking mentoring and small seed grants
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: Women and underrepresented student, faculty, and community entrepreneurs in Champaign-Urbana
deadline_note: No current application cycle found. The NSF pilot award (#1464507) ran October 2015 to March 2019; latest AWARE prize evidence found is a 2020 award reported in 2021.
notes: The official page researchpark.illinois.edu/AWARE returns 404, and AWARE does not appear on the current Research Park resources page or EnterpriseWorks incubator page. No 2026 activity found; program may be dormant or folded into other offerings (e.g. an AWARE award tied to the Cozad New Venture Competition in 2021). Name appears as both 'Accelerating' and 'Advancing' in sources.

name: Catherine and Don Kleinmuntz Center for Genomics in Business and Society
description: A donor-funded center at IGB that supports turning genomics research into real-world impact, with proof-of-concept awards for faculty and a summer innovation program for grad students and postdocs. Its website shows no news after 2022, so current activity is uncertain.
good_for: Proof-of-concept funding for IGB genomics research
parent_org: Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology (IGB)
ideal_participant: IGB faculty (Mikashi Awards); IGB grad students and postdocs (Young Innovator Program, PSCB seminars)
deadline_note: Programs page lists no deadlines. Last posted application call was for the 2022 Young Innovator Program (March 2022).
cost_or_funding: Mikashi Awards: up to two awards per year of $50,000 to $75,000 for up to two years; Young Innovator Program: tiered awards of $5,000 to $20,000 to three cohort members (per https://kleinmuntzcenter.illinois.edu/programs; currency of these amounts unverified)
notes: Map lists it as 'Kleinmuntz Center' under IGB; full name is the Catherine and Don Kleinmuntz Center for Genomics in Business and Society. News stops in 2022; the Young Innovator Program may have been folded into or superseded by the IGB Early Innovator Program (similar 10-week summer format), but no page confirms this. Possibly dormant.

name: EnterpriseWorks Catapult New Venture Program
description: A competitive award from EnterpriseWorks that pays most of the cost of early professional services, such as legal setup, bookkeeping, SBIR applications, and branding, for a University of Illinois affiliated startup that is just forming. Winners also become EnterpriseWorks incubator tenants.
good_for: Covering legal and setup costs when forming a university-linked startup
ideal_participant: Pre-formation University of Illinois affiliated founders, including Cozad student teams, with technology licensed or being licensed from UIUC
deadline_note: Applications reviewed on a rolling basis per the program page. Student teams have also received it as a Cozad New Venture Challenge award.
cost_or_funding: EnterpriseWorks covers 80% of service costs up to $5,000 for one year (per program page); awardees must become EnterpriseWorks tenants
notes: Status evidence: Research Park article dated August 21, 2026 lists the Catapult New Venture Program among current incubator programs; April 28, 2025 article reports 2025 Cozad teams receiving Catapult Awards. Program page is dated January 29, 2021, so terms may be outdated, but the program is named in 2025 and 2026 Research Park news. Not on the map's EnterpriseWorks or Research Park lists. The related Student Startup Tenancy award is likely covered by the map's 'Incubator labs, offices, & maker space' entry.

name: Illinois Innovation Award
description: An annual Grainger Engineering award that honors a UIUC student whose innovation or translational research could have major real-world impact. Students are nominated by a campus unit, faculty member, or mentor, and the winner receives $20,000 and a trophy.
good_for: Recognition and cash for a high-impact student innovation
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship (Grainger College of Engineering)
ideal_participant: Full-time on-campus UIUC students with an impactful innovation or research translation, nominated by a mentor or unit
deadline_note: Per program page, nominations open Fall 2026 and recipients are announced at a Spring 2027 ceremony; no specific nomination deadline is stated.
cost_or_funding: $20,000 award plus trophy (per program page)
notes: Status evidence: Program page describes the 2026-2027 cycle: nominations open Fall 2026, awards announced Spring 2027. Page is titled Illinois Innovation Award & Fiddler Innovation Fellowship. Self-nomination is not allowed; each unit can submit up to two nominations.

name: Illinois Proof-of-Concept Program (IPOC)
description: An Office of Technology Management grant of up to $50,000 that helps Illinois faculty researchers push a disclosed invention toward a product, with funds able to pay student researchers on the project.
good_for: Funding faculty-led work to prove an invention is commercially viable
ideal_participant: Full-time Illinois academic researchers (or emeritus faculty with active labs) with an invention report on file at OTM; students can be paid on projects
deadline_note: 2026 application window closed (deadline was Feb 27, 2026); awards announced May 2026. Next cycle dates not yet posted.
cost_or_funding: Up to $50,000 per project, paid in tranches (per OTM IPOC page)
notes: Status evidence: OTM IPOC page shows a 2026 funding cycle (now closed) with awards announced May 2026 for summer 2026 projects. Students cannot apply as PI but can be paid from awards. The Feb 27, 2026 deadline came from search-result summary of an OTM page; the fetched page confirms only that the 2026 window closed. General OTM email: otm@illinois.edu.

name: Illinois Ventures
description: The University of Illinois System's affiliated venture investor, which backs early-stage deep tech startups with university ties through a Deep Tech Fund, a Pre-Seed Fund, and an alumni Angel Network.
good_for: Raising seed or pre-seed equity for a university-connected tech startup
ideal_participant: Founders of high-growth tech startups with a University of Illinois connection, including student and faculty teams
deadline_note: Pitches accepted via contact form; no deadline.
notes: Offices in Champaign and Chicago. No contact email listed; contact form at /prospective-companies. Investment sizes are not published. The map lists an Illinois Ventures Evergreen Fund. No official Illinois Ventures page found on 2026-10-13 mentions it (the site lists a Deep Tech Fund, a Pre-Seed Fund, and an Angel Network), so it is merged here until someone confirms it exists.

name: Brand Hub Professional Online Certificates and Development
description: Listed on the ecosystem map as Brand Hub's professional online certificate and development offerings in branding and advertising. No current official page describing these certificates could be reached.
good_for: Learning branding and advertising skills online
parent_org: Hub for Brand Innovation and Advertising Technology (Brand Hub)
ideal_participant: Students and professionals wanting branding and advertising training
notes: Brand Hub site unreachable (DNS failure on 2026-10-13); no certificate page found. The College of Media separately offers online graduate certificates in Strategic Brand Communication and an online MS in Strategic Brand Communication (listed at online.illinois.edu), which may be what this entry refers to or its successor; these are paid academic programs, not Brand Hub branded. Consider merging into brand-hub or dropping.

name: Design Thinking Courses (DTX)
description: Siebel Center for Design teaches DTX courses open to students from any background, from Introduction to Design Thinking and Human-Centered Design Across Disciplines to special topics in UX and AI, plus an Innovation Studio capstone. There is also an interdisciplinary certificate in Health Innovation.
good_for: Learning human-centered design and user research for credit
ideal_participant: Undergraduates from any major wanting design thinking, UX, and innovation skills
notes: Status evidence: Courses page lists Fall 2026 DTX offerings (DTX 180, 221, 251, 495, 499). DTX 180 satisfies a Gen Ed Social and Behavioral Sciences requirement. DTX 499 Innovation Studio no longer requires instructor approval. Health Innovation certificate is 9 credits. Full list at catalog.illinois.edu/courses-of-instruction/dtx/.

name: Entrepreneurs Without Borders
description: A Gies program where students do service-learning projects that support entrepreneurship education and small or social enterprises in low-income communities abroad, with recent projects in Argentina, Tanzania, and South Africa. It grows out of the Subsistence Marketplaces Initiative.
good_for: Global social entrepreneurship and international service learning
parent_org: Illinois Social Innovation / Subsistence Marketplaces Initiative, Gies College of Business
ideal_participant: UIUC students interested in international development and social enterprise
notes: Dedicated page pages.business.illinois.edu/subsistence/.../entrepreneurs-without-borders/ failed to resolve (DNS error), so the old link appears broken. No dates, costs, or eligibility found on official pages.

name: Entrepreneurship Courses (Gies)
description: Gies offers a set of entrepreneurship courses, including Introduction to Entrepreneurship (BADM 346), New Venture Creation (BADM 446), Legal Issues in Entrepreneurship, Entrepreneurial Finance, and Venture Capital. Many count toward the campus-wide Entrepreneurship Minor, which is open to most undergraduates.
good_for: Learning startup fundamentals for credit
ideal_participant: Undergraduates from any major wanting formal entrepreneurship coursework
notes: Status evidence: Courses listed in the 2026-2027 Academic Catalog. No single official 'Entrepreneurship Courses' page found; URL points to the catalog list. Per search snippet, the Entrepreneurship Minor (16 hours, core BADM 346 and TE 250) is open to all UIUC undergrads except SIE majors. BADM 445 Small Business Consulting is marked 'no longer offered' on its Gies course page though still in the catalog.

name: Entrepreneurship Courses, Certificates, & Advising (Landuyt Center)
description: Landuyt's TE entrepreneurship courses, undergraduate and graduate certificates, and a graduate concentration in entrepreneurship. Students can also meet with peer and academic advisors about startup ideas and course planning.
good_for: Learning entrepreneurship for credit and earning a certificate
ideal_participant: Any UIUC student who wants entrepreneurship coursework or a credential, plus advising on ideas
deadline_note: Landuyt calendar lists Mar 1, 2027 as the application deadline for the Graduate Concentration in Entrepreneurship and Innovation. Undergraduate certificate page lists submission deadlines of Jan 15, Jun 1, and Sep 1 (no year) and says to apply before the start of your final semester.
notes: Status evidence: Courses page lists TE offerings for Fall 2026 and Spring 2027; Landuyt calendar lists Academics Open Office Hours Oct to Dec 2026. Undergrad certificates: Innovation (11 hrs) and Technology Commercialization (5+ hrs, open to any major); an AI and Machine Learning Focus certificate is listed without details. Separate graduate certificates and a graduate concentration exist. Peer advising page said to check back in September to book.

name: Illinois I-Corps (NSF I-Corps, Great Lakes Hub)
description: UIUC's I-Corps site teaches faculty and student researchers customer discovery so they can test whether their research can become a product, and it serves as a path into the NSF National I-Corps program. Offerings include a workshop series, the free I-Corps Boost program, and SBIR/STTR proposal help.
good_for: Testing whether a research idea has a market
subcategory: Customer discovery and research commercialization training
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship (part of NSF Great Lakes Regional I-Corps Hub)
ideal_participant: Faculty, grad students, and researchers with lab technology to commercialize
deadline_note: No cohort dates or deadlines listed on the official site.
cost_or_funding: I-Corps Boost is free (per programs page); other costs not stated
notes: Status evidence: Illinois I-Corps site shows impact statistics as of February 2026; the program is linked from the current Landuyt programs page. Site still uses the old Technology Entrepreneur Center branding and tec@illinois.edu. Program contact listed as Morgan Malm (mmalm@illinois.edu). Regional hub site greatlakesicorps.org returned 403 when fetched. National I-Corps requires NSF-funded research ties.

name: Illinois Reboot: A Coding Pre-Academy
description: A free, virtual intro data science course for career changers in Central Illinois, run by Research Park with American Family Insurance. Research Park has since retired the program.
good_for: Historical reference only; the program has been retired
ideal_participant: Was aimed at Central Illinois adults changing careers into tech, not at enrolled UIUC students
deadline_note: Cohorts ran from 2021 to 2022, and a fourth cohort was announced for March 2022. No current cohort.
cost_or_funding: Was free to participants
notes: Status evidence: The Research Park events page lists ILLINOIS REBOOT Coding Pre-Academy with the notice 'Illinois Reboot has been retired.' Defunct. Research Park lists the program as retired. A follow-on course, Illinois Reboot 2.0 (Python Project Course), also ran and has closed. Recommend removing this entry from the student directory or marking it archived.

name: Innovation, Leadership & Engineering Entrepreneurship (ILEE) B.S. Dual Degree
description: A second bachelor's degree for Grainger engineering students that adds 31 credit hours of innovation, leadership, and entrepreneurship coursework on top of the primary major. Students finish both degrees within 10 semesters.
good_for: Engineers who want a full degree in entrepreneurship and leadership
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship (Grainger College of Engineering)
ideal_participant: Grainger engineering undergraduates in good standing (2.25+ GPA) who have taken at least one TE course
deadline_note: Landuyt calendar lists application deadlines of Nov 1, 2026 and Apr 1, 2027. Must apply no later than the semester before your final year.
notes: Status evidence: Landuyt events calendar lists ILEE Dual Degree application deadlines on Nov 1, 2026 and Apr 1, 2027. Open to all engineering majors including ABE and ChemE. Deadlines come from the Landuyt Center's official events calendar, not the degree page itself.

name: Research Park Workforce Development
description: Research Park offers professional development workshops, mentorship, and networking events for employees of tenant companies, including the many student interns who work there. It is a benefit for companies and their staff rather than a program students apply to.
good_for: Professional development for Research Park employees and interns
ideal_participant: Research Park and EnterpriseWorks companies and their employees, including student interns already working there
notes: No dedicated page exists. Affiliation Benefits lists professional development workshops, recruiting assistance, mentorship, and networking events for Research Park companies and their employees. Bryan Goode, Talent Manager, leads workforce development and recruitment per the team page. Interns may join through their employer, which is why student_eligible is Varies. Consider merging with research-park-recruitment-services.

name: Strategy, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship Major (BS)
description: A Gies bachelor's degree focused on starting, financing, and managing new ventures and innovation. Beyond the business core, students take courses like Introduction to Entrepreneurship and New Venture Creation plus skill-building and experiential electives such as iVenture seminars.
good_for: Earning a business degree centered on entrepreneurship
ideal_participant: Gies undergraduates (or dual-degree seekers) who want an entrepreneurship-focused major
notes: Status evidence: Listed in the 2026-2027 Academic Catalog (catalog.illinois.edu). 124 hours minimum; 57-hour business core plus 28 hours of major core and electives. Major core: BADM 341, 346, 367, 446. Non-Gies students should consider the Entrepreneurship Minor instead (SIE majors are not eligible for that minor).

name: Assessment and Research Team (Siebel Center for Design)
description: The Siebel Center for Design's research group, founded in 2019, studies how human-centered design is taught, learned, and used, and publishes findings at conferences and in journals. Undergraduate and graduate students can join projects as Research Scholars.
good_for: Students wanting research experience in human-centered design
ideal_participant: Undergrad or grad students from any discipline interested in design research
notes: The SCD site now calls this the 'Assessment and Research team' rather than 'Assessment & Research Lab'; led by Dr. Saadeddine Shehab. No dated 2026 projects listed on the research page, though SCD hosts 'Research and Reflections 2026'. Overlaps with the SCD Scholars resource (Research Scholars).

name: City Scholars & Startup City Scholars
description: Grainger juniors and seniors spend a semester in Chicago taking UIUC classes while interning at a tech company. A Startup City Scholars track had students build ventures through UChicago Polsky's College New Venture Challenge.
good_for: Spending a semester in Chicago's tech and startup scene
subcategory: Chicago semester internship and startup program
parent_org: Grainger College of Engineering (with DPI, UIC, UChicago Polsky Center)
ideal_participant: Junior or senior CS, CS + X, CompE, or EE students (3.2 GPA recommended) for City Scholars; student founders for the startup track
deadline_note: Spring 2027 City Scholars applications closed Sep 13, 2026 (per application page); accepted candidates may withdraw until Nov 8, 2026. Program runs Jan 19 to May 5, 2027. No Startup City Scholars dates found.
notes: Status evidence: Application page lists Spring 2027 cohort: applications Aug 24 to Sep 13, 2026, program Jan 19 to May 5, 2027. Startup track last seen in Landuyt news dated Mar 10, 2025. Two tracks. City Scholars (internship track) is well documented on the official site. Startup City Scholars (entrepreneurship track) is not mentioned on the current City Scholars site; it appears only in news (Landuyt, Mar 2025) describing a nine-week Chicago cohort feeding into UChicago's CNVC, where Grainger awarded a $75,000 prize pool. Startup track status for 2027 is unverified.

name: Fiddler Innovation Fellowship
description: An annual NCSA fellowship, funded by an endowment from Jerry Fiddler and Melissa Alden through the eDream Institute, that recognizes Illinois students and faculty proposing creative interdisciplinary projects mixing art, science, and technology. Fellows receive funding and work with NCSA mentors or collaborators.
good_for: Funding a creative art and technology project
ideal_participant: Illinois students and faculty with interdisciplinary art, science, and technology projects
deadline_note: No deadline posted. 2026 fellowship awarded April 17, 2026. Endowment page links a faculty fellowship application at edream.illinois.edu/apply-fiddler-fellowship/.
cost_or_funding: 2026 fellowship award was $10,000 (per https://www.ncsa.illinois.edu/2026/05/04/ncsa-awards-2026-fiddler-innovation-fellowship/); amounts have varied by year and level
notes: Status evidence: NCSA announced the 2026 Fiddler Innovation Fellowship winner, awarded at an April 17, 2026 ceremony (news post dated May 4, 2026). Format appears to vary year to year: 2025 cohort honored 38 students (many via SPIN and Design for America), while 2026 named a single $10,000 winner from four finalists. Endowment also funds fellowships for SPIN undergraduate interns. Contact is Olena Kindratenko, Assistant Director for Research and Education.

name: Orange & Blue Ventures
description: A new Gies College of Business program where students run a venture capital investing effort, investing real money in startups with advice from faculty and industry professionals. Students learn deal sourcing and investing while building relationships with founders.
good_for: Hands-on venture investing experience as a student
parent_org: Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, Gies College of Business
ideal_participant: Business students interested in venture capital (eligibility not yet published)
deadline_note: Launching Fall 2026 per Gies. No application dates published.
notes: Status evidence: Gies Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship page says the program is launching in Fall 2026. Brand new program; led by Rob Metzger, clinical professor of finance. The listed email is aimed at prospective partner funds; students are pointed to students.giesbusiness.illinois.edu. Eligible majors, fund size, and application process not stated.

name: Research Park Company Internships
description: More than 120 companies at Research Park, including corporate innovation centers and startups, hire UIUC students for paid internships next to campus. Students work part time during the semester and full time in summer, and they apply to each company directly through the Research Park job board.
good_for: Paid part-time tech and business work near campus
subcategory: Paid student internships at Research Park companies
ideal_participant: UIUC undergraduate and graduate students of any major who want paid industry experience during the school year
deadline_note: Hiring happens year round, with the most postings in early fall (August to September) and early winter (December to January), per the internship FAQ.
cost_or_funding: Paid positions; the FAQ says all Research Park internships and jobs are paid
notes: The FAQ says interns typically work 10 to 15 hours a week during the semester. International students should check with ISSS first. Each company hires independently, and there is no shared application. The job board loads postings dynamically, so I could not see current 2026 postings to confirm activity. uirp-jobs@illinois.edu is the job board posting address, per a Research Park page in search results. The general contact is research-park@illinois.edu.

name: SCD Research and Practice Scholars
description: Students at the Siebel Center for Design can join as Research Scholars, helping study how human-centered design is taught and used, or Practice Scholars, helping run courses, workshops, and curriculum. It is a way to gain hands-on research or teaching experience in design.
good_for: Research or teaching experience in human-centered design
ideal_participant: UIUC students interested in design research or design education
deadline_note: Applications via interest forms; no deadlines listed.
notes: No SCD 'Fellows' student program found; 'Fellow' appears only as a staff title on the team page. Program now named 'Research and Practice Scholars'. Over thirty scholars to date per the page.

name: Alchemy Technology Foundry
description: A UIUC deep tech foundry led by ECE professor Sanjay Patel where student teams built technology for real problems, including parts of the Safer Illinois app. Students got hands-on product engineering experience on faculty-guided projects.
good_for: Building deep tech products on a faculty-led student team
parent_org: Grainger College of Engineering (ECE), associated with Landuyt Center
ideal_participant: Engineering and CS students who want to build technology on a faculty-led team
notes: Possibly defunct. The official domain alchemyfoundry.com lapsed (302 to hugedomains.com). Alchemy is not listed on the current Landuyt Center programs or collaborations pages. A LinkedIn result shows Patel's Alchemy role ending January 2024 (not verified). No current official page found; url points to the director's homepage.

name: Champaign-Urbana Community Fab Lab
description: A community makerspace on the UIUC campus with free open hours where students and local residents can use fabrication tools, get design help, and take workshops. It also runs youth summer camps and rents equipment by appointment.
good_for: Hands-on fabrication and making with community support
ideal_participant: Students and community members who want to learn fabrication or build a physical prototype
notes: Status evidence: Summer Camps page lists 2026 camps running June 8 to August 7, 2026; homepage lists current fall open hours. Fall open hours: Sundays 1 to 5 PM, Monday to Thursday 5 to 9 PM, at 1301 S. Goodwin Ave, Urbana (MC-615). Opened in 2009. Some appointment-based rentals carry small hourly fees (search snippet cited $1/hour for electronics prototyping), not verified on a fetched page. Affiliated with the iSchool per a 2023 Daily Illini article.

name: ECE Open Lab
description: A student-run makerspace in the ECE Building where students can work on personal and student org hardware projects outside of coursework. It has tools for 3D printing, PCB work, soldering, and CNC milling, with volunteer lab monitors on shift.
good_for: Building hardware and electronics prototypes
parent_org: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
ideal_participant: Students from any major building personal or RSO hardware projects
notes: Located in Room 2024 ECEB, 306 N Wright St, Urbana. Site says open 24/7 with lab access and lists monitor shifts 1 to 9 PM; it is calling for lab monitor applicants. The site's about-us.html page returns 404. Not for homework. No dated 2026 activity found.

name: Health Maker Lab
description: A Carle Illinois network of about 19 campus fabrication and design labs that helps medical students team up with engineering, business, and science peers to prototype healthcare solutions. It also offers guidance on design, prototyping, IP, and invention disclosure, and runs the Health Make-A-Thon.
good_for: Finding prototyping labs and support for a health innovation
ideal_participant: Medical students and their interdisciplinary teammates building health technology
notes: Member labs include the Grainger IDEA Lab, CU Community Fab Lab, Illinois Maker Lab, MechSE MakerWorks, Siebel Center for Design, and EnterpriseWorks. Most recent listed event is a December 2025 patient-centered Make-a-Thon. Eligibility for non-medical students is not stated.

name: IDEA Lab at Grainger Engineering Library
description: A creative technology space in the Grainger Engineering Library with bookable group project rooms, loanable VR and AR gear, podcasting equipment, and 3D printing and scanning. Open to students, faculty, and staff of all majors, it is a handy place to build early prototypes and work as a team.
good_for: Team workspace and quick 3D printing or VR prototyping
ideal_participant: Any UIUC student, staff, or faculty member who needs team space or creative tech
notes: Official page now expands the name as Innovation and Design in Engineering and the Arts; the ecosystem map uses Innovation, Discovery, Design, and Data. A May 2026 Daily Illini article (secondary) describes it as currently operating. Search results mention idealab@library.illinois.edu as a contact, but the official About page lists only staff emails (coordinator Stuart Turner, slturne1@illinois.edu). Located at 1301 W. Springfield Ave., Urbana.

name: Illinois MakerLab
description: A 3D printing lab in the Gies Business Instructional Facility, billed as the first business school 3D printing lab. Students and faculty can get 3D printing and design help, take courses and workshops, and order prints online.
good_for: Quick 3D printed prototypes and learning digital fabrication
ideal_participant: UIUC students and faculty who need to 3D print a prototype or learn 3D design
notes: Status evidence: Homepage banner reads 'FALL 2026 NOW OPEN' (makerlab.illinois.edu). Official name styled 'Illinois MakerLab'. Room 3030, Business Instructional Facility, 515 E. Gregory Dr., Champaign; open about 30 hours/week. Search results showed uimakerlab@illinois.edu but not confirmed on a fetched official page. Also runs summer camps and related courses (e.g. BADM 331 Making Things, BADM 357 Digital Making Seminar).

name: Jackson Innovation Studio (MechSE MakerWorks)
description: A makerspace in the Sidney Lu Mechanical Engineering Building with 3D printers, laser cutters, hand tools, and machines that students can use for class or personal projects. Students can build physical prototypes cheaply, paying only for filament or bringing their own laser cutting material.
good_for: Building low-cost physical prototypes
parent_org: Department of Mechanical Science and Engineering, Grainger College of Engineering
ideal_participant: Students building hardware prototypes; undergrads who volunteer get 24/7 access
cost_or_funding: 3D printing filament charged per gram (PLA $0.03/g); laser cutters free but bring your own material (per studio page)
notes: Status evidence: Official studio page links a Spring 2026 Awards Banquet Program and shows a 2026 copyright. Open 11am to 10pm weekdays per the page, open to students, staff, faculty, and community. MechSE design courses get laser cutter priority over personal use. Wood Maker Studio restricted to trained volunteers and design class students. MakerWorks Club volunteers (UIUC undergrads) get 24/7 access and up to $50 per semester in free materials. Page does not mention entrepreneurship directly.

name: Siebel Center for Design
description: A campus design hub that teaches human-centered design through courses, certificates, and workshops, and runs a makerspace with laser, CNC, 3D printing, electronics, and textiles labs. Students can learn design thinking, prototype in The Shop, and book studio and event space.
good_for: Learning design thinking and prototyping a product
ideal_participant: Students of any major who want design skills or a place to build prototypes
deadline_note: See the Siebel Center for Design workshops entry for upcoming maker workshops.
notes: Status evidence: designcenter.illinois.edu lists upcoming 2026 events, e.g. Intro to Lasers workshop Oct 19, 2026 and Intro to Print Lab Nov 2, 2026. Many programs (SHIFT) target educators rather than founders; makerspace and HCD workshops are most relevant to student founders.

name: The Shop (Siebel Center for Design)
description: The Shop is SCD's makerspace with labs for 3D printing, laser cutting, CNC, woodworking, electronics, textiles, and printmaking. Students get trained on tools during Training Days and then build their own projects during Production Days.
good_for: Building physical prototypes with shop tools
ideal_participant: Students building hardware or physical prototypes who want access to fabrication tools and training
deadline_note: Open during fall and spring semesters (Tue to Sun, various hours); closed in summer.
notes: Status evidence: SCD workshops page lists Maker Workshops held at The Shop on Oct 19, Oct 26, and Nov 2, 2026. Located at 1208 S. Fourth St., Champaign. Monday reserved for registered Maker Workshops.

name: Translational Research Facility
description: Listed on the UIUC ecosystem map as an internal partner, but no UIUC facility by this exact name could be found on official pages. Related translational spaces include the Cancer Center at Illinois Biomedical Research Center at Carle and the Carle Illinois Translational Oncology and Regenerative Medicine (TORM) lab.
good_for: Unclear; needs verification
ideal_participant: Biomedical researchers moving work toward clinical use (if the facility exists as listed)
notes: Map entry has no link. Multiple searches and the Carle Illinois research facilities page show no facility named 'Translational Research Facility'. Candidates: CCIL Biomedical Research Center (3rd floor, Mills Breast Cancer Institute, Urbana), the TORM lab at Beckman Institute (announced 2026), or a planned biomedical translational building referenced in an older system hub page. Consider dropping or relabeling once identified.

name: AxisMED
description: A student-led biomedical pre-incubator at Carle Illinois that puts students from different majors on teams to develop a healthcare venture over the academic year. Teams follow a condensed version of the Stanford Biodesign process with five design review checkpoints and get ready for campus startup competitions.
good_for: Building a medical device or health venture with an interdisciplinary team
ideal_participant: Medical, graduate, and undergraduate students interested in building healthcare technology ventures
deadline_note: Program runs fall to spring per the Carle Illinois page; no 2026-27 application dates are posted.
notes: Founded 2021 by Carle Illinois medical students. A team (AMELIA) won $10,000 at the 2024 Cozad New Venture Challenge, which is a competition prize, not an AxisMED grant. An NCSA spotlight says AxisMED gives micro-grants for prototyping, but the official page does not confirm amounts. axismed.org returned no readable content.

name: CUBE Consulting
description: Champaign-Urbana Business and Engineering (CUBE) Consulting is a student-run consultancy where teams do business strategy, engineering, and design projects for real clients each semester. Members get hands-on client experience plus case training, and no prior consulting background is needed.
good_for: Getting real client consulting experience across business, engineering, and design
ideal_participant: Undergraduates of any major and year who want client consulting experience
deadline_note: Fall 2026 first-round applications closed Aug 28, 2026 per https://www.cubeconsulting.org/join-us; next cycle (likely Spring 2027) not yet posted.
notes: Status evidence: Join Us page lists a Fall 2026 recruitment timeline, with first-round applications due Aug 28, 2026 and final decisions Sep 10, 2026. Running since 2012 and described as the first US Junior Enterprise. Site says any major and any year (freshman to senior) may apply.

name: EntreCORPS
description: A student-run, pro bono consulting group at Gies that gives early-stage startups research-backed strategy, growth, and technology advice. Students join as consultants to get real project and team-management experience, and campus startups can request free help.
good_for: Free startup consulting, or consulting experience for students
parent_org: Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, Gies College of Business
ideal_participant: Students wanting startup consulting experience; early-stage startups in the Illinois ecosystem needing strategy help
deadline_note: Past cycles had deadlines around late January to Feb 1 (e.g. Feb 1, 2025 per a Gies social post); no current deadline found on an official page.
cost_or_funding: Free (pro bono) for client startups per giesgroups.illinois.edu/entrecorps/home/
notes: Merged OVAEL program listing and student org listing into one resource. The old entrecorps.illinois.edu/apply page references Spring 2019 and is outdated. Site says 90+ clients served.

name: Founders: Illinois Entrepreneurs
description: A long-running student entrepreneurship club at UIUC that connects aspiring founders with mentors, potential cofounders, and startup competitions. It is a low-barrier way for students at any stage to meet other builders and find campus resources.
good_for: Meeting cofounders and other student entrepreneurs
ideal_participant: Any UIUC student curious about starting or growing a business
notes: Former site founders.illinois.edu fails with a TLS certificate error (points at GitHub Pages), so it looks broken. The OneIllinois RSO page lists 7 officers but shows no upcoming events. LinkedIn gives a founding year of 2013. Do not confuse this club with Founders Week (Sep 30 to Oct 3, 2026), which is run by Entrepreneurship at Illinois, not this RSO. RSO listings now live on one.illinois.edu rather than campuslabs engage.

name: Illinois Business Consulting (IBC)
description: A large student-run, professionally managed consulting organization at Gies where students work in teams on semester-long paid projects for clients ranging from startups to large companies and nonprofits. Members get real consulting experience and exposure to how businesses, including young startups, solve problems.
good_for: Getting real client consulting experience, including with startups
ideal_participant: Students who want consulting experience on real business problems
notes: Gies page says 260+ members and 500+ clients including startups. Founding year conflicts (1995 per U.S. News vs 1996 per IBC About page). U.S. News says members come from Gies and other colleges, but the official page does not state eligibility. Comparable to OTCR and CUBE, which are on the map.

name: Illinois Enactus
description: A student social entrepreneurship group that builds small ventures tackling social and environmental problems in Champaign-Urbana, then hands them off to community partners. Members work on real projects such as STEM access for girls and language help for immigrants.
good_for: Building a social impact venture with a team
parent_org: Registered student organization, UIUC (Enactus network chapter)
ideal_participant: Freshmen, sophomores, and juniors of any major interested in social impact
deadline_note: Fall 2026 recruiting has closed per https://www.illinoisenactus.com/. Recruitment is usually the third week of the fall and spring semesters; Spring 2027 dates not posted.
notes: Status evidence: Homepage says the Fall 2026 recruiting cycle has ended and lists six current projects. LinkedIn describes it as a 501(c)(3) non-profit. Seniors appear not to be eligible per the homepage.

name: OTCR Consulting
description: A long-running student-run consulting firm at UIUC that takes on business strategy and technology projects for clients ranging from local startups to large companies. Members get real client work and a large alumni network.
good_for: Real client consulting experience in business and technology strategy
parent_org: Registered student organization, UIUC (Gies student groups)
ideal_participant: Undergraduates, mostly business and engineering, interested in consulting careers
notes: otcr.illinois.edu and www.otcr.illinois.edu do not resolve (DNS failure), so the old domain appears dead. The giesgroups.illinois.edu/otcr pages exist in search results but returned no readable content when fetched. Sources give founding year as 1999 or 2000. Specializes in business strategy, technology strategy, and technology implementation per search snippets.

name: Product Space UIUC
description: A student organization that trains members in product management, product marketing, and product design through a fellowship, then puts them on semester-long projects building real products with companies. It also runs a product hackathon where design, product, and engineering students build and present.
good_for: Learning to build and ship products the way a startup PM does
ideal_participant: Students of any major who want product management or product design skills for a startup or tech career
deadline_note: An Instagram post said Fall 2026 applications opened August 17. A product hackathon was listed for early October 2026 (sources conflict: Oct 10 on the chapter events page vs Sep 29 to Oct 5 on Devpost). Next listed event is an internal member event on October 27, 2026.
notes: Status evidence: OneIllinois chapter page lists a Product Space Internal Event on October 27, 2026; the official About page carries a September 2026 date and 2026 copyright. Founded August 2023. Site says all majors welcome. No contact email published; site links Instagram and LinkedIn only. Hackathon is low/no-code and limited to UIUC students per Devpost listing (page returned 403 to direct fetch; details from search snippet).

name: Venture Capital Association (Illini VCA)
description: A student organization that teaches venture capital through an eight-week analyst bootcamp ending in a Shark Tank style competition, then places selected members on projects with real VC firms. Students learn how investors evaluate startups, which helps both future founders and future investors.
good_for: Learning how investors judge startups and working on real VC projects
ideal_participant: Students interested in venture capital or in understanding how startups raise money
deadline_note: Fall 2026 Analyst Bootcamp meets Tuesdays 6:30 to 7:30 pm, October 13 to November 17, 2026. Spring 2026 recruitment closed February 13, 2026 per the group's recruitment page (secondary snippet).
notes: Status evidence: OneIllinois page lists VCA Fall 2026 Analyst Bootcamp weekly meetings on Tuesdays from October 13 through November 17, 2026. Two tracks: Analyst Bootcamp, then a more selective Associate Program working alongside VC firms. illinivca.com did not resolve; illinivca.org shows only the name. Do not confuse with the Chicago-based Illinois Venture Capital Association (IVCA), a trade group.

name: Zero2One
description: A student-run startup incubator at UIUC that coaches early-stage student founders through a semester-long cohort ending in a pitch competition. It has also hosted Launchpad, a campus-wide student startup pitch event.
good_for: Developing a student startup idea in a semester cohort
ideal_participant: Students of any major with an early startup idea
deadline_note: Website still advertises the Fall 2024 incubator; no 2026 cohort or Launchpad dates found.
notes: Possibly winding down or rebranded. The site is branded Zero2One VC and its newest content is Fall 2024. One LinkedIn page is labeled 'Old Page - No Longer Active' (a newer Zero2One VC LinkedIn page exists). The OneIllinois RSO page shows only 3 officers and 5 members and no upcoming events. A 2024 YouTube listing cited a $1000+ Launchpad prize pool (secondary source, not used in cost field). Founded around 2020 per MechSE news.

name: AgTech Innovation Summit
description: A free one-day conference at Research Park, presented with Bayer, where agriculture researchers, startups, investors, and industry leaders meet for panels, fireside chats, and networking. Students interested in agtech can hear from industry leaders and watch a regional startup pitch competition.
good_for: Meeting agtech companies and investors
ideal_participant: Students, researchers, and founders working on agriculture or food technology who want industry and investor contacts
deadline_note: The 2026 summit was held March 10, 2026. The 2027 date has not been announced. Recent summits have been held in March as part of Champaign-Urbana AgTech Week.
notes: Status evidence: The 11th annual summit took place March 10, 2026 at the Illinois Conference Center in Champaign, per the Research Park AgTech Summit 2026 page. The Research Park site also uses the shorter name 'AgTech Summit'. Search snippets say the conference is free because sponsors cover it, but the 2026 page I fetched does not state cost. The Startup World Cup Agriculture and Food Regional pitch competition was held at the 2026 summit.

name: Brand Hub Workshops and Seminars
description: Brand Hub has run workshops, speaker talks, and seminar series on branding and advertising, such as Brand Ambassador workshops and an Emerging Leaders series with industry speakers. The only events found date from 2021 to 2023.
good_for: Learning branding from industry speakers
parent_org: Hub for Brand Innovation and Advertising Technology (Brand Hub)
ideal_participant: Students interested in branding, marketing, and advertising
notes: Events URL taken from search results; brandhub.illinois.edu failed DNS lookup on 2026-10-13, so it could not be loaded. Search snippet indicated the events page listed only 2021 to 2023 events. Likely inactive; consider merging into brand-hub. Former official URL https://brandhub.illinois.edu/events/ did not resolve (DNS failure) on 2026-10-13.

name: Catalyze: Professional Networking Event
description: An evening networking event at EnterpriseWorks where local tech companies, from startups to large firms, meet job seekers in an informal setting. Students and others can meet Research Park and Champaign-Urbana employers and learn about full-time roles.
good_for: Meeting local tech employers informally
ideal_participant: Job seekers, including graduating students, looking to connect with Champaign-Urbana tech companies
deadline_note: The Research Park events page says it is held every fall and spring. The only dated editions found are October 26, 2021 and a Wednesday, Nov. 2 event with no year shown (likely 2022). No 2025 or 2026 date was found.
notes: The event page shows no year and appears to date from about 2022. It is co-presented by Research Park, Champaign County EDC, and You're Welcome CU. The page names Carly McCroy (carly@champaigncountyedc.org) and Emily Neal (ewick@illinois.edu) as contacts, and both may be out of date. The events page still lists Catalyze without a retired notice. The event may be dormant.

name: CEO and Founders Roundtable
description: An invitation-only quarterly dinner where about 25 to 30 CEOs of Champaign-Urbana tech companies, from early-stage startups to established firms, compare notes on running a business. Research Park funds it, and it is free for participants.
good_for: Peer learning among local tech CEOs
ideal_participant: CEOs and founders of Champaign-Urbana tech companies, including EnterpriseWorks startups. Student founders would need an invitation.
deadline_note: The page says it meets quarterly but lists no upcoming dates.
cost_or_funding: Free to participants; funded by University of Illinois Research Park, LLC (per the roundtable page)
notes: The official name is now 'CEO and Founders Roundtable'. The ecosystem map calls it 'Champaign-Urbana CEO Roundtable'. It started in 2005, and Chinmay Soman has chaired it since 2020. The page says to contact Laura Appenzeller but lists the address lfrerich@illinois.edu, which may be outdated. The page appeared to be about two years old. The map lists this item twice (map-027 and map-106), both under this id.

name: CU Women in Tech
description: An informal networking forum at Research Park for women in Champaign-Urbana's tech sector, held several times a year with a talk by an accomplished local leader. Attendees meet other women in tech and hear about speakers' careers.
good_for: Networking with women in the local tech industry
ideal_participant: Women working in technology in Champaign-Urbana. Students may be able to attend, but the page does not say.
deadline_note: The event page says it happens several times a year, and the events listing says quarterly. The most recent event listed was in April 2025 with Gies Dean Brooke Elliott. No 2026 dates were found.
notes: The events listing calls it 'Women in Tech' and says it is held quarterly. The event page says several times a year. A related ISTC listing ('Women in CU Tech Industry Lunch Forum') names Laura Frerichs (lfrerich@illinois.edu) as a contact.

name: Founders Week
description: The flagship annual week of events from Entrepreneurship at Illinois that brings students, founders, investors, and campus programs together for talks, a founder showcase, and networking. Students get a concentrated look at the whole campus startup ecosystem in a few days.
good_for: Meeting the whole Illinois startup ecosystem in one week
parent_org: Entrepreneurship at Illinois (Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation)
ideal_participant: Any student curious about startups, plus founders looking for investors and partners
deadline_note: 2026 edition ran September 30 to October 3, 2026 per the official page. No 2027 dates posted yet.
notes: Status evidence: Official Founders Week page says the third annual Founders Week ran September 30 to October 3, 2026, and lists 2026 sponsors. Not on the ecosystem map list itself. The official page mixes a past-tense 2026 recap with an older 'sign up for Founders Week 2026' section, so parts of the page are stale. 2025 edition included a Capital Forum and Founder Showcase; about 500 attendees per a linked story. Sponsors include EnterpriseWorks, Gies, iVenture, Illinois Ventures, and Research Park.

name: Innovation Celebration
description: An awards event hosted by the Champaign County EDC with UIUC and Parkland College that honored local entrepreneurs, innovators, and supporters of the regional startup economy. It has not been held since 2019.
good_for: Historical reference only; not currently running
ideal_participant: Local entrepreneurs and innovation supporters (when held)
deadline_note: Last held 2019; 2020 event postponed indefinitely per https://innovationcelebration.com/.
notes: Status evidence: innovationcelebration.com shows the last held event in 2019 and a March 11, 2020 notice postponing the 15th annual event (April 1, 2020) to a date never announced. Likely defunct: no event since 2019 and the 2020 edition was postponed indefinitely. The EDC page still describes it but lists no dates. Recommend removing from active listings or marking discontinued.

name: Innovation Expo
description: A resource fair where UIUC entrepreneurs, designers, and innovators could meet campus programs and organizations that support startups. It was co-hosted by the Technology Entrepreneur Center, Innovation LLC, and Founders.
good_for: Discovering campus startup resources in one place
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship, Founders, Innovation LLC
ideal_participant: Students new to entrepreneurship looking for resources
deadline_note: Last known event: Sep 29, 2020 (virtual, free).
cost_or_funding: Free admission (2020 listing)
notes: Possibly discontinued or replaced; no 2021 to 2026 listings found. Founders Week (Sep 30 to Oct 3, 2026) and the TE 200 Idea Fair are the closest current events. No dedicated official page exists; url is the 2020 calendar entry.

name: Innovation Living-Learning Community
description: A residential community in Townsend Hall (Illinois Street Residence Halls) where students of any major live together, take TE 200, and use a shared project space called The Garage. Staff connect residents with mentors, funding, and events on innovation and entrepreneurship.
good_for: Living with other student builders in your first year
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship & University Housing
ideal_participant: Undergraduates, especially first-years, of any major interested in innovation
deadline_note: Housing page lists a May 8 priority deadline for the housing contract and LLC essay; no year stated.
notes: Housing page says floors 3 to 5 of Townsend Hall; Landuyt page says Illinois Street Residence Halls (Townsend is part of ISR). First-year residents must take TE 200. Housing cost is standard University Housing rates (not stated on page).

name: Pygmalion Festival
description: An annual multi-day arts and culture festival in Champaign-Urbana featuring music, comedy, literature, film, and food. In past years it included a tech track with a startup demo night, a hackathon, and tech crawls, but no tech programming was found for 2026.
good_for: Local community networking at a major C-U festival
ideal_participant: Students and community members interested in C-U culture and the local tech scene
deadline_note: 2026 festival took place September 24 to 27, 2026 per https://thisispygmalion.com/.
notes: Status evidence: Official site lists the 2026 festival as September 24 to 27, 2026 in Urbana. The festival is active, but the Pygmalion Tech Festival component (Tech Demo at Krannert, PygHack hackathon, Tech Crawl, Research Park panels) appears only in roughly 2016 to 2019 sources. The 2026 official site and coverage mention music, comedy, literature, film, and food, not tech. The tech track is likely discontinued; consider relabeling or dropping from an entrepreneurship directory.

name: Research Park Entrepreneurship Workshops
description: Research Park and EnterpriseWorks host workshops on startup topics such as IP, pitching, customer discovery, pricing and sales, fundraising, and SBIR/STTR, plus recurring meetups and founder breakfasts at EnterpriseWorks.
good_for: Learning startup basics and meeting local founders
parent_org: Research Park at the University of Illinois (EnterpriseWorks)
ideal_participant: Students, researchers, and early founders in Champaign-Urbana building a startup
deadline_note: No entrepreneurship workshops were listed on the EnterpriseWorks calendar for October to December 2026 (checked 2026-10-13). The workshops page itself is dated January 2019.
notes: Status evidence: Research Park events calendar (calendars.illinois.edu/list/5115) lists EnterpriseWorks meetups Oct to Dec 2026, e.g. Champaign Blockchain Meetup Oct 16, 2026 and First Friday Breakfast Nov 6, 2026. Merged: the ecosystem map lists 'Entrepreneurship Workshops' under both EnterpriseWorks and Research Park. EnterpriseWorks is Research Park's incubator, and both point to the same single Workshops page and one shared events calendar run by Research Park, so this is treated as one series. next_deadline reflects the next calendar meetup, not a formal workshop; the First Friday Breakfasts are for EnterpriseWorks startups only.

name: Siebel Center for Design Workshops
description: SCD runs human-centered design workshops, which student groups can schedule, and hands-on Maker Workshops in The Shop such as laser cutting and sticker printing. It also offers SHIFT sessions for educators.
good_for: Short, hands-on intros to design thinking and maker tools
ideal_participant: Students or student orgs wanting a quick, practical intro to design methods or fabrication tools
deadline_note: Event: Intro to Lasers student maker workshop, Oct 19, 2026, in The Shop (per SCD homepage). SHIFT Max (for educators) applications run Feb 1 to Mar 8, 2027.
notes: Status evidence: Workshops page lists upcoming fall 2026 sessions (e.g. Oct 15 SHIFT Spark, Oct 19 Intro to Lasers at The Shop). SHIFT Spark and SHIFT Max are aimed at educators, not students. HCD Workshops for student orgs at /outreach/HCDWorkshops.

name: Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Workshop
description: A January winter break trip to Silicon Valley where about 25 selected UIUC students meet founders, venture capitalists, corporate leaders, and alumni. The Landuyt Center arranges airfare, lodging, and most meals, with donor support covering much of the cost.
good_for: Seeing Silicon Valley startups and investors up close
ideal_participant: Full-time, on-campus UIUC students curious about startups and tech careers
deadline_note: Applications for the January 2027 workshop are closed (per program page). Applications open each fall; applicants are notified in early October and finalists interview. Next cycle (January 2028) dates not posted.
cost_or_funding: Participant fee required, financial support available; airfare, lodging, and most meals arranged (per program page)
notes: Status evidence: Program page says applications are closed for the January 2027 workshop. Online degree students are not eligible. Counts as an elective option for the Technology Commercialization certificate.

name: SocialFuse
description: A recurring Landuyt Center mixer where students can pitch an idea, find teammates for a startup, or just network and watch. Staff also answer questions about the Cozad New Venture Challenge.
good_for: Finding cofounders and practicing a quick pitch
ideal_participant: Students looking for teammates or wanting to share an early idea
deadline_note: Event: next SocialFuse is Nov 5, 2026, 5:00 to 7:00 pm, Campus Instructional Facility. RSVP at https://forms.illinois.edu/sec/510096211.
notes: Status evidence: Landuyt events calendar lists SocialFuse Fall26 on Nov 5, 2026, 5:00 to 7:00 pm at the Campus Instructional Facility. Spring edition paired with Cozad Info Night (Jan 28, 2026 in last cycle). Counts as an approved event for the Innovation certificate.

name: Designer-in-Residence Program
description: EnterpriseWorks startups can get free design guidance from industrial design professor Deana McDonagh, covering user research, empathic design, early form exploration, and design strategy for their product.
good_for: Improving a product's user experience with design thinking
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: Startups housed in EnterpriseWorks developing a physical or user-facing product
deadline_note: Requests by online form; no deadline.
cost_or_funding: No charge for EnterpriseWorks companies (per program page)
notes: Eligibility is limited to EnterpriseWorks companies, so students qualify only if their startup is a tenant or affiliate. Contact is the general Research Park email.

name: Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR) Program
description: Free one-on-one consulting from experienced entrepreneurs on topics like fundraising, team building, value proposition, marketing, and investor readiness, plus monthly training sessions on IP, sales, and SBIR grant writing.
good_for: Getting free advice from seasoned founders on an early-stage startup
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: UIUC students, faculty, and staff, Research Park clients, or community tech entrepreneurs with an early-stage idea or startup
deadline_note: Appointments requested by online form; no deadline.
cost_or_funding: Free consulting (per program page)
notes: Program page dated 2021, but the program is still linked from current EnterpriseWorks pages. Status left Unknown since no dated 2026 EIR activity was found.

name: Illinois FAST Center (SBIR/STTR Assistance)
description: An EnterpriseWorks-led program that helps Illinois small businesses and researchers win federal SBIR and STTR grants through free workshops, office hours, one-on-one mentoring, and proposal reviews.
good_for: Writing a competitive SBIR or STTR grant proposal
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, Research Park at the University of Illinois
ideal_participant: Founders, researchers, and inventors anywhere in Illinois preparing an SBIR or STTR proposal
deadline_note: Workshop series (READY!, SET!, GO!) dates are posted on the events calendar; none found for Oct to Dec 2026. GO! phase listed as not yet scheduled.
cost_or_funding: Free workshops; 1:1 help limited per business and dependent on program funding (per FAST Center page)
notes: The URL linked from the incubator page footer (researchpark.illinois.edu/fast-center-at-illinois-sbir-resources/) returns 404; the working page is /resources/illinois-fast-center/. Impact stats on the page appear to be unfilled placeholders (0 clients, $0M).

name: Intellectual Property Clinic
description: A spring-semester clinic where College of Law students, supervised by a patent attorney, draft patent applications or prepare trademark filings for selected UIUC student startups. Students get legal work worth thousands of dollars for free, paying only USPTO filing fees.
good_for: Getting a patent or trademark application drafted for free
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship & College of Law
ideal_participant: Student entrepreneurs with an invention or brand to protect
deadline_note: Clinic runs in spring only. Page lists an info night on Thurs., Oct. 8 (year not stated, likely 2026 and now past); no application deadline stated.
cost_or_funding: Free legal services; students pay USPTO filing fees (per program page)
notes: Two tracks: Patent and Trademark. Launched in 2008 with Adjunct Prof. Joseph Barich. Patent track companies get preference for the trademark track.

name: Office of Technology Management (OTM)
description: The campus office that receives invention disclosures, files patents, and licenses University of Illinois technologies to companies, including startups founded on university research. Students and researchers whose idea came out of university work use it to report the innovation and work out ownership and licensing.
good_for: Disclosing and licensing a university invention
parent_org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation
ideal_participant: Faculty, staff, and students with an invention or software developed using university resources
deadline_note: Disclosures accepted on a rolling basis via the Report Your Innovation page.
notes: Merged the map entries 'Office of Technology Management' and 'Disclosure & Licensing Information' (OTM section) into one resource; disclosure page is https://otm.illinois.edu/researchers-innovators/report-your-innovation. Office is clearly operating (2025 stats), but no 2026-dated evidence was found on the homepage, so status left Unknown. Student relevance depends on whether IP arose from university resources or employment.

name: Cancer Center at Illinois (CCIL)
description: An NCI-designated cancer research center at UIUC that funds engineering and data science approaches to cancer with seed grants and training programs. It has no startup program, but it connects researchers with Carle clinicians and translational research space.
good_for: Cancer technology research connections and seed grants for member teams
ideal_participant: Researchers and students working on cancer-related technology, diagnostics, or therapies
deadline_note: 2026 seed grant proposals were due March 11, 2026 (per search summary of CCIL seed grant info; not directly fetched).
notes: Status evidence: Homepage shows news dated October 8, 2026 and October 7, 2026. No entrepreneurship or commercialization program was found on the homepage. Grant programs (Seed, Bridge, Planning, High-Throughput Screening) are research grants that require Cancer Center membership. Student training includes a Cancer Education Undergraduate Certificate and graduate TiME Program. Publishes an 'Innovation Insider' newsletter.

name: Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology (IGB)
description: A campus genomics and life sciences institute with a bioeconomy and entrepreneurship arm, including a summer Early Innovator Program and a lecture series. Grad students and postdocs in related research can get commercialization training, mentors, and small proof-of-concept prizes.
good_for: Turning life science research into a startup
subcategory: Research institute with bioeconomy and entrepreneurship programs
ideal_participant: Graduate students, postdocs, and faculty doing biology or genomics research with commercial potential
deadline_note: Early Innovator Program runs 10 weeks starting the week of May 19 through end of July; page gives no year or application deadline.
cost_or_funding: Early Innovator Program top pitch winners receive up to $5,000 in proof-of-concept funding (per https://www.igb.illinois.edu/bioeconomy/igb-early-innovator-program)
notes: Status evidence: IGB homepage shows an October 2026 events calendar and Woese Prize nominations due November 15, 2026 (institute activity, not entrepreneurship-specific). Bioeconomy contact listed as Tracy Parish, Director of External Relations and Strategic Partnerships (tparish@illinois.edu). Early Innovator Program is open to University of Illinois grad students and postdocs whose work relates to an IGB theme. A search snippet from entrepreneurship.illinois.edu news referenced a 2026 Early Innovator pitch contest, not directly verified.

name: Carle Illinois College of Medicine (CI MED)
description: UIUC's engineering-based medical school, whose Office of Research and Innovation runs the Health Make-A-Thon, innovation seed grants, and medical device regulatory advising. Most funding and advising is reserved for CI MED students, though some events involve interdisciplinary student teams.
good_for: Health and medical device innovation
ideal_participant: CI MED students and faculty; other students interested in health tech via Make-A-Thon teams
deadline_note: Health Innovation Research Day was held April 3, 2026.
cost_or_funding: For CI MED students: Maker Coin of $10,000 per student across four categories; Research and Innovation Pathway Grants up to $3,000 per project (per https://medicine.illinois.edu/research-and-innovation)
notes: Status evidence: Research and Innovation page announces Health Innovation Research Day on April 3, 2026; CI MED 2026 graduation news published. Health Make-A-Thon and Health Maker Lab appear as separate map entries. Regulatory and development advising contact: yschleif@illinois.edu (CI MED faculty and students).

name: Corporate Innovation Centers
description: About 30 companies, including Fortune 500 firms, run innovation centers at Research Park to work with university faculty and hire student teams on real product and research projects. For students, these centers are the main source of paid internships and full-time job offers next to campus.
good_for: Working on industry R&D teams while in school
ideal_participant: Companies looking to open a campus innovation center. Students reach these centers through internships.
notes: Status evidence: The Research Park homepage shows 2026 news posts, including August 2026 items. The Corporate Innovation page currently markets the program to companies. This is a service for companies, which apply to become tenants. The page says more than 800 students work at Research Park year round. The figure of about 30 innovation centers comes from the student internship FAQ. Students reach these centers through the internships entry. Status evidence is park-wide activity, not a program-specific 2026 item.

name: Corporate Startup Intros
description: Research Park staff introduce startups, especially EnterpriseWorks companies, to corporations with innovation centers at the park, which can lead to partners, pilot customers, or investors. No official page describes how the service works.
good_for: Startups seeking corporate partners or pilot customers
ideal_participant: Founders of startups at EnterpriseWorks or Research Park looking for corporate partners. This is not a program students apply to directly.
notes: I found no dedicated page or formal program named 'Corporate Startup Intros' on the Research Park site. The URL points to the team page because it lists Bailey Conrady, Associate Director of Community and Industry Partnerships (edenbur2@illinois.edu), the closest match for this service. The description is inferred from the ecosystem map label. Consider merging this into research-park-corporate-innovation-centers.

name: Gies College of Business
description: UIUC's business college, home of the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, which runs the iVenture Accelerator, EntreCorps consulting, and a student venture fund. Students get entrepreneurship coursework, including a minor offered jointly with Grainger, plus access to accelerator and investing programs.
good_for: Business-side entrepreneurship classes, accelerator, and student VC
ideal_participant: Students of any major interested in the business side of starting a company
notes: Status evidence: Gies Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship page says Orange and Blue Ventures is launching in Fall 2026. Umbrella college; entrepreneurship programs are run through the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship (see ovael).

name: Hub for Brand Innovation and Advertising Technology (Brand Hub)
description: A College of Media unit, created by the Sandage Department of Advertising, the Siebel Center for Design, and Technology Services, that matched student teams with organizations on branding projects. Its website no longer loads, so it may be inactive.
good_for: Getting student help with startup branding and advertising
parent_org: Charles H. Sandage Department of Advertising, College of Media
ideal_participant: Startups needing branding or advertising help; advertising students seeking client projects
notes: Possibly defunct: brandhub.illinois.edu failed DNS lookup (ENOTFOUND) on 2026-10-13, and the newest Brand Hub items found in search date to roughly 2023 to 2024 (Brand Ambassador Program, events page listing 2021 to 2023 events). Contact email from cached site info only. Former official URL https://brandhub.illinois.edu/ did not resolve (DNS failure) on 2026-10-13.

name: Illinois Social Innovation
description: A campus-wide Gies initiative that trains students to tackle social and environmental problems through social entrepreneurship coursework, global programs, and hands-on impact projects. Participants can access mini-grants, seed capital eligibility, mentoring, and credit-bearing consulting projects.
good_for: Students building ventures or projects with a social impact mission
parent_org: Gies College of Business (Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship)
ideal_participant: UIUC students interested in social entrepreneurship and changemaking, from any major
notes: Program areas listed: Social Entrepreneurship Coursework, Global Entrepreneurship, Inclusive Entrepreneurship, Action Learning for Social Impact, Social Innovation Design Lab. Events and News sections were empty; no dated 2026 activity found. A newer OVAEL program list names Social Innovation Global Scholars rather than ISI itself, so ISI may now function as an umbrella brand. The School of Social Work also has an Illinois Social Innovation page.

name: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship
description: Grainger Engineering's entrepreneurship center, formerly the Technology Entrepreneur Center (TEC). It runs the Cozad New Venture Challenge, I-Corps, an IP clinic, startup advising, and entrepreneurship courses and certificates.
good_for: Taking entrepreneurship courses and entering campus startup competitions
ideal_participant: Any UIUC student exploring a startup idea or entrepreneurship coursework
cost_or_funding: Cozad New Venture Challenge has awarded $5M+ since 2000 (per landuyt.illinois.edu)
notes: Status evidence: landuyt.illinois.edu lists Oct 12, 2026 news naming seven Tech Startup Challenge finalists and Aug 27, 2026 news on expanding to Chicago. Renamed from Technology Entrepreneur Center (TEC). tec.illinois.edu still works and 301-redirects to https://landuyt.illinois.edu. Executive director Jed Taylor is also Grainger's Assistant Dean for Innovation and Entrepreneurship. The map also lists Grainger's Office of the Associate Dean for Innovation & Entrepreneurship. That role is now titled Assistant Dean for Innovation and Entrepreneurship, is held by the Landuyt Center director, and has no separate office page, so it is merged into this entry.

name: National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA)
description: UIUC's supercomputing and data science center, which works with companies through an Industry Partner Program and runs student programs such as the SPIN undergraduate internship and the Fiddler Innovation Fellowship. Student founders can tap its computing resources, experts, and industry network.
good_for: Access to advanced computing, AI expertise, and industry partners
subcategory: Supercomputing center with industry and student programs
