ideal_participant: Students and researchers building AI, data, or compute-heavy projects, and companies seeking research partnerships
notes: Status evidence: NCSA Industry Conference 2026 held October 13 to 14, 2026 (publish.illinois.edu/ncsa-industry-2026); NCSA news posts from May and August 2026. Industry partnerships contact listed as NCSA-Industry@mx.uillinois.edu; conference page lists industry@ncsa.illinois.edu. No startup-specific NCSA program was found; Industry Partner Program targets organizations. Student offerings include SPIN (spin.ncsa.illinois.edu).

name: Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation (OVCRI)
description: The campus office that oversees research and innovation at UIUC, including technology transfer, Research Park, EnterpriseWorks, and I-Corps, and that co-organizes Founders Week. Students and researchers can use it as a gateway to invention disclosure, startup handbooks, and entrepreneurship events.
good_for: Commercializing university research and finding campus startup support
ideal_participant: Graduate students and faculty with research they want to commercialize
notes: Status evidence: research.illinois.edu news covers Founders Week 2026 (Sept 30 to Oct 3) and the April 2026 Cozad New Venture Challenge. Owns and operates EnterpriseWorks (per Aug 21, 2026 Research Park article). Founders Week 2026 already took place Sept 30 to Oct 3, 2026.

name: Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship
description: Gies Business's entrepreneurship hub, now presented as the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship. It runs the iVenture Accelerator, the EntreCORPS student consulting group, and student investing programs, and supports the entrepreneurship minor.
good_for: Joining a student startup accelerator or student VC fund
ideal_participant: UIUC students building a startup or wanting hands-on venture experience
cost_or_funding: iVenture Accelerator provides resources up to $20,000 (per giesbusiness.illinois.edu/origin-ventures-office-of-entrepreneurship)
notes: Status evidence: Official page says Orange and Blue Ventures is launching in Fall 2026. Naming: the Origin Ventures Academy for Entrepreneurial Leadership (OVAEL, est. 2004 as the Academy for Entrepreneurial Leadership, renamed 2018) was expanded into the Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship, announced April 21, 2025. The announcement frames it as an expansion, not an explicit rename, but the current official page uses only the Office name and does not mention OVAEL. The old giesgroups.illinois.edu/ovael page returned no meaningful content. No email on the page; phone 217-300-7327.

name: Research Park at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
description: A university technology park in Champaign with 100+ companies, the EnterpriseWorks incubator, and entrepreneurs-in-residence. Students can find paid internships at corporate and startup tenants, and founders can get incubation and startup support.
good_for: Finding tech internships and startup incubation near campus
parent_org: Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation
ideal_participant: Students seeking internships and founders looking for incubation and corporate connections
notes: Status evidence: Homepage lists 2026 news items including Sep 23 podcast and Aug 21 'named a top incubator and accelerator'. Homepage reports 350+ startups nurtured. AgTech Summit and Founders Week listed without dates.

name: Research Park Recruitment Services
description: Research Park helps its tenant companies recruit UIUC students through a job board, career fair, and campus recruiting events. The service is for companies, so students benefit through the postings and employer events.
good_for: Companies hiring UIUC student talent
subcategory: Talent recruiting support for tenant companies
ideal_participant: Research Park and EnterpriseWorks companies, including student-founded startups at EnterpriseWorks, that need to hire. Students looking for jobs should use the internships entry.
notes: No dedicated page exists. The Affiliation Benefits page lists 'recruiting assistance' as a tenant benefit. The team page lists Bryan Goode, Talent Manager (bdgoode@illinois.edu), for workforce development and recruitment. Consider merging with research-park-workforce-development.

name: The Grainger College of Engineering
description: UIUC's engineering college, which houses the Landuyt Center and backs student startup programs such as the Cozad New Venture Challenge and the Grainger Engineering Tech Startup Challenge. Students get entrepreneurship courses, certificates, an engineering entrepreneurship dual degree, and pitch opportunities.
good_for: Finding engineering entrepreneurship courses, degrees, and startup competitions
ideal_participant: Engineering students interested in starting a company or studying entrepreneurship
cost_or_funding: Grainger Engineering Tech Startup Challenge offers a prize pool of over $200,000 (per grainger.illinois.edu/academics/entrepreneurship)
notes: Status evidence: Grainger entrepreneurship page shows Aug 27, 2026 news on Landuyt Center expanding to Chicago and an Oct 13, 2026 Q&A story. Umbrella college; the entrepreneurship programs themselves are mostly run by the Landuyt Center. Map links the general college site; the entrepreneurship page is more useful for founders. The university research calendar lists the Tech Startup Challenge at the Chicago Venture Summit on Oct 20, 2026.

name: Champaign County Economic Development Corporation
description: A public-private economic development group for Champaign County that hosts the Illinois Small Business Development Center, which gives free, confidential business advising. It also runs small business funding programs with local cities and helps companies with sites, data, and local connections.
good_for: Free small business advising and local business funding programs
ideal_participant: Student founders forming a local business in Champaign County
cost_or_funding: SBDC advising is offered at no cost per https://www.champaigncountyedc.org/
notes: Status evidence: City of Champaign announcement dated Sept 17, 2026 says the city and CCEDC launched a third round of the New and Growing Business Programs (seen in search results; page blocked direct fetch). CCEDC also named a new SBDC director in May 2026 per search results. Office at 1817 S. Neil St, Suite 100, Champaign. Also runs Made in Champaign County and C-U AgTech Week, and is involved in the iFAB biomanufacturing Tech Hub. The EDC site's own news feed was last updated July 2024. Footer email domain is .com while staff emails use .org.

name: Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE)
description: A Midwest quantum consortium of universities (including Illinois), national labs, and companies, based at UChicago. Students can use its talent portal and internship listings and apply to its undergraduate research fellowship.
good_for: Quantum careers, internships, and research fellowships
parent_org: University of Chicago (Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering)
ideal_participant: Students and founders in quantum science and engineering
notes: Status evidence: CQE homepage shows multiple October 2026 news items. UIUC is a placement site for OQI fellows and IQUIST helped fund the Summer 2024 OQI program. Q-Ready (free, for students in IL, WI, IN) seen only in search snippets, not verified on an official page. UIUC member status not clearly labeled on homepage.

name: Discovery Partners Institute (DPI)
description: The University of Illinois System's Chicago institute connecting university research with industry around AI and tech talent. For UIUC students the main route in is the Grainger City Scholars program, a paid semester internship in Chicago.
good_for: Spending a semester working in Chicago tech
subcategory: University of Illinois System Chicago institute
ideal_participant: Junior or senior CS, CE, CS+X, or EE students wanting Chicago tech experience
deadline_note: City Scholars Spring 2027 applications closed September 13, 2026; matches announced by November 18, 2026; internships run January 20 to May 5, 2027 (per City Scholars site).
cost_or_funding: City Scholars internships pay $25 to $45 per hour, 20 hours per week (per City Scholars site)
notes: Status evidence: DPI homepage shows a September 20, 2026 Chicago Tribune op-ed; City Scholars application page shows a Spring 2027 cohort with applications August 24 to September 13, 2026. DPI's other talent programs target K-12 and community college students. City Scholars is run by Grainger and hosted at DPI; it may deserve its own directory entry. No email listed; contact via https://dpi.illinois.edu/about/contact.

name: Duality Quantum Accelerator
description: A Chicago accelerator for quantum and related deep-tech startups, led by UChicago's Polsky Center and the Chicago Quantum Exchange with UIUC as a founding partner. Its site now says Duality is part of Alchemist Chicago.
good_for: Launching a quantum hardware or software startup
parent_org: Polsky Center (UChicago) and Chicago Quantum Exchange
ideal_participant: Founders of early-stage quantum technology startups
deadline_note: Most recent round (via Alchemist Chicago) closed August 14, 2026 per https://www.dualityaccelerator.com/about/.
notes: Status evidence: Duality about page states Alchemist Chicago applications are open and close August 14, 2026. POSSIBLE RESTRUCTURE: Duality site says Alchemist Chicago 'now includes Duality' and describes an Alchemist Accelerator partnership, so Duality may now run as a track within Alchemist Chicago. Founding partners: UIUC, Argonne, P33. Funding and equity terms not stated on current pages. Earlier cohorts (2024) required a U.S. legal entity and part-time Chicago presence; may not apply now.

name: Engineering Innovation Leadership Council (EILC)
description: An invitation-only national network of engineering college research and entrepreneurship leaders (associate deans and center directors) that holds workshops on strengthening innovation at universities. It offers nothing students can join; any benefit to UIUC students is indirect.
good_for: Context on national engineering innovation leadership networks
parent_org: VentureWell (event host); Grainger listed as participant
ideal_participant: Engineering deans and innovation center directors
deadline_note: Most recent event found: national workshop June 12, 2024 at the University of Maryland.
notes: The ecosystem map labels it with NSF, but the VentureWell event page names no funder and does not mention Illinois. No official EILC homepage found; the only page is the 2024 VentureWell event page. No activity after 2024 found.

name: Entrepreneurial Living-Learning Community (ELLC) Roundtable
description: An annual gathering, started by Illinois in 2012, where staff and faculty who run entrepreneurship-themed residence hall communities at different universities swap practices. It is a staff network, so UIUC students benefit only indirectly through the Innovation Living-Learning Community.
good_for: Background on the network behind entrepreneurship residence communities
subcategory: National roundtable for living-learning community leaders
ideal_participant: Staff running or planning entrepreneurship living-learning communities
notes: Landuyt collaborations page describes it as annual since 2012 but it no longer appears in the collaborations navigation. All found editions (Atlanta, Gainesville, UW-Madison) are several years old; no 2025 or 2026 edition found. No dedicated page or contact.

name: IBM-Illinois Discovery Accelerator Institute
description: An IBM and Grainger research partnership focused on AI systems and quantum computing. It is not a startup program; students mainly benefit by joining faculty research projects or attending its seminars.
good_for: Research exposure in AI and quantum computing with IBM
parent_org: IBM and The Grainger College of Engineering
ideal_participant: Grad students and faculty in AI, quantum, and systems research
notes: Status evidence: IBM newsroom announced the renewal and expansion on April 16, 2026. Despite the name, this is a research institute, not a startup accelerator. The ISUR page states the IIDAI Undergraduate Research Experience was canceled. Homepage links an Externship page whose details were not checked. Contact is via web form only.

name: Illinois AgTech Accelerator
description: A Champaign agtech accelerator at Research Park, led by gener8tor with Serra Ventures, that ran a 12-week investment program and a 7-week no-equity gBETA program. The most recent cohort found was in 2023.
good_for: Early-stage agriculture and food tech startups
parent_org: gener8tor and Serra Ventures, with University of Illinois Research Park
ideal_participant: Founders of early-stage agtech or food tech startups, including student founders with a working product
deadline_note: The latest cohorts found were the spring 2023 gener8tor AgTech cohort (started March 20, 2023) and the fall 2023 gBETA AgTech cohort (started October 2, 2023). No 2024 to 2026 cohort or application call was found.
notes: Possibly dormant. The newest official evidence is a 2023 cohort, and gener8tor's /agtech page returned 404. Coverage from 2020 and 2023 says gener8tor AgTech startups received a $100,000 investment, but this is not confirmed for current cohorts, so I left cost_or_funding blank. A search snippet said the accelerator took part in CU AgTech Week in March 2026, but the 2026 events page I fetched did not mention it. The URL is a 2023 Research Park news post because no current program page was found.

name: Illinois Innovation Network (IIN)
description: A University of Illinois System network of research and innovation hubs, including one at UIUC, that runs seed grants and an annual conference. Students can attend the conference free and senior undergrads and grad students can present posters.
good_for: Statewide innovation networking and presenting research
ideal_participant: Researchers and students interested in statewide innovation and economic development
deadline_note: Registration for the Oct 22 to 23, 2026 conference at SIUE closes Oct 15, 2026; student poster session Oct 23 (per conference page). Presentation proposals closed July 15, 2026.
cost_or_funding: Conference registration free for students, $20 for general attendees (per conference page)
notes: Status evidence: 2026 IIN Conference scheduled October 22 to 23, 2026 at SIUE; IIN Council met September 17, 2026; 2026-27 Fellows announced May 7, 2026. Location is statewide Illinois (closest allowed value used). Seed grant and Fellows eligibility not verified.

name: Illinois Small Business Development Center at Champaign County EDC
description: A state and SBA funded advising center that gives free one-on-one business advising, workshops, and help with business plans, government contracting, and international trade. A student starting a real business can book an appointment for planning and launch help.
good_for: Free one-on-one help writing a business plan or launching a small business
parent_org: Champaign County Economic Development Corporation (host); Illinois DCEO and U.S. SBA (funders)
ideal_participant: Students or community members starting or running a for-profit small business in Champaign County
deadline_note: Event: 2026 Fall/Winter Open Office Hours, Nov 12, 2026, 12 to 3 pm (per cusbdc.org). Advising is by appointment year round.
cost_or_funding: Advising offered at no cost (per cusbdc.org)
notes: Status evidence: Official cusbdc.org events listing shows a 2026 Fall/Winter Open Office Hours on November 12; City of Champaign September 17, 2026 release refers applicants to the SBDC. Hosted by the Champaign County EDC (which is on the map as its own entry) at 1817 S. Neil St, Suite 100, Champaign. Services are for legal US residents and citizens per cusbdc.org, which may exclude some international students. Not student specific. Includes an International Trade Center. Search results cite a May 2026 CCEDC announcement naming Lauren Gramly as director (not fetched directly).

name: Illinois University Incubator Network (IUIN)
description: A statewide network of university incubators, led by EnterpriseWorks, that shares resources among incubator managers. Students get little directly, but a UIUC founder can use it to find sister incubators across Illinois.
good_for: Finding university incubators elsewhere in Illinois
parent_org: EnterpriseWorks, University of Illinois Research Park
ideal_participant: Incubator staff; founders looking for incubators across Illinois
notes: The Research Park page https://researchpark.illinois.edu/incubator-network/ returns 404. Most recent dated item on illinoisincubators.org is the 2024 America's Seed Fund Road Tour; no 2025 or 2026 activity found. Location is statewide Illinois (closest allowed value used).

name: Jump ARCHES (Applied Research for Community Health through Engineering and Simulation)
description: A partnership of OSF HealthCare, Grainger's Health Care Engineering Systems Center, and UI College of Medicine Peoria that funds engineer and clinician research teams. Grants go to faculty, but students can join funded projects or apply to its summer internship.
good_for: Medical device and simulation research with clinicians
parent_org: Health Care Engineering Systems Center (Grainger) and OSF HealthCare Jump Simulation
ideal_participant: Grainger faculty with an OSF clinical partner; students seeking health tech research or internships
deadline_note: Event: Health Care Engineering Systems Symposium, Oct 27, 2026, Jump Trading Simulation & Education Center, Peoria. Spring 2026 grant proposals closed April 10, 2026.
notes: Status evidence: Spring 2026 grant call (due April 10, 2026) posted by Illinois CSBS; OSF lists the Health Care Engineering Systems Symposium on Tuesday, October 27, 2026 in Peoria. Each proposal needs one Grainger investigator and one OSF or UICOMP investigator. Program reports 154 projects funded and $11 million awarded. Award amounts are in the Award Guidelines document, not checked. Symposium audience and cost not stated.

name: Kern Entrepreneurial Engineering Network (KEEN)
description: A national network of engineering schools, funded by the Kern Family Foundation, that promotes an entrepreneurial mindset in engineering teaching. Grainger is a partner, so students benefit through KEEN-influenced courses rather than applying to anything.
good_for: Understanding the entrepreneurial mindset framework behind some Grainger courses
parent_org: Kern Family Foundation (Grainger College of Engineering is a partner)
ideal_participant: Faculty designing engineering courses; students see the effects indirectly
notes: Status evidence: Grainger's 2025-26 Strategic Instructional Innovations Program project and a Siebel School article describe current course work aligned with the KEEN Mindset Framework. Grainger partnership announced September 21, 2020, led by Andrew Singer and Jonathan Makela. KEEN's own site (Engineering Unleashed) did not render via fetch, so the URL and any student-facing offerings are unverified. This is mainly a faculty network.

name: Mayo Clinic & Illinois Alliance for Technology-Based Healthcare
description: A research and education partnership between Mayo Clinic and the University of Illinois that connects Illinois engineers and scientists with Mayo clinicians. Students can apply to its graduate fellowship and summer research programs at Mayo.
good_for: Health tech research experience with Mayo Clinic clinicians
parent_org: Mayo Clinic and University of Illinois (overseen by the Interdisciplinary Health Sciences Institute)
ideal_participant: UIUC grad students in health tech research; undergrads seeking summer research at Mayo
deadline_note: Graduate fellowship applications are rolling and depend on available funds per the fellowship page. No dates listed for summer programs.
cost_or_funding: Graduate fellowship: $40,000 annual stipend, tuition and listed fees, partial health insurance; travel and Mayo housing are the student's responsibility (per fellowship page)
notes: Status evidence: About page lists a 2024 ARPA-H award of up to $33 million for the MarginDx project; graduate fellowship page states applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Graduate fellowship requires current UIUC grad enrollment with at least two years remaining and at least 12 months in residence at Mayo in Rochester, MN. Undergraduate programs listed: SURF, HERE, CRISP; computational genomics summer course at IGB. Fellowship contact LeaAnn Carson (lcarson@illinois.edu).

name: Midwest Engineering Entrepreneurship Network (MEEN)
description: A network of more than 30 Midwest universities' technology entrepreneurship programs, co-founded by Illinois and Michigan, that holds an annual conference for staff and faculty to share practices. Students do not participate directly; the benefit is indirect, through better programs at the Landuyt Center.
good_for: Context on how Midwest engineering entrepreneurship programs collaborate
parent_org: Landuyt Center for Entrepreneurship and University of Michigan Center for Entrepreneurship
ideal_participant: University administrators, faculty, and staff in technology entrepreneurship
deadline_note: 2026 conference held July 13 to 14, 2026 at UChicago; 2027 dates not posted.
cost_or_funding: No conference attendance fee; attendees pay own travel and lodging (per MEEN site)
notes: Status evidence: MEEN site lists the 2026 conference July 13 to 14, hosted by the University of Chicago (registration closed). Founding year conflict: MEEN site says 2011, Landuyt collaborations page says 2001. Contacts listed on MEEN site: Matthew Lynall (mlynall@purdue.edu) and Chris Eakin (ceakin@umich.edu). Location is Midwest regional.

name: Polsky Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation
description: UChicago's entrepreneurship and tech transfer center, which runs the New Venture Challenge, the Polsky Exchange coworking space, and Duality. Most programs are for UChicago affiliates; UIUC students mainly benefit from open events and joint programs.
good_for: Chicago startup events and connections
ideal_participant: UIUC founders building connections in Chicago
deadline_note: Upcoming Polsky dates on the homepage are mostly for UChicago students (for example, PE/VC Lab applications due October 16 for Booth MBAs).
notes: Status evidence: Polsky homepage lists October 2026 events, including an October 16 PE/VC Lab deadline and an October 15 Business Acumen session. Absorbed the former Chicago Innovation Exchange in 2016 (now Polsky Exchange, 1452 E 53rd St). Also runs Third Coast Foundry with other Midwest universities. Homepage does not say which programs are open to non-UChicago students. No general email listed; main phone 773.834.4525. The map lists the Chicago Innovation Exchange (CIE) & Illinois Partnership separately. CIE became part of the Polsky Center in 2016 (now Polsky Exchange), and the Illinois partnership page dates from about 2016, so it is merged here.

name: ThinkChicago
description: A talent program led by World Business Chicago with the City of Chicago and the University of Illinois System that brought students to Chicago for company tours and networking. No current event with dates was found.
good_for: Exploring Chicago tech careers and companies
ideal_participant: STEM students considering a Chicago tech career
deadline_note: Site mentions a community college event on October 30 with no year; most recent flagship event shown is ThinkChicago Lollapalooza 2023.
notes: Site footer shows copyright 2015 and the latest dated event is 2023, so activity in 2025 or 2026 is unconfirmed. Past Lollapalooza cohorts were application and invitation only. Colleges contact: tdunn@worldbusinesschicago.com.

name: University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: The University of Illinois System's Chicago campus, with its own innovation center, incubator, and entrepreneurship courses. Almost all of it is for UIC students, so UIUC students mainly connect through joint programs like City Scholars.
good_for: Chicago connections within the University of Illinois System
ideal_participant: UIC affiliates; UIUC founders looking for Chicago-area partners or system-wide programs
notes: UIC OTM services page shows most programs (Innovation Center incubation, MADLab, OTM, UICentre, CCTS) are UIC-only. Exceptions: the UIC Entrepreneurial Support Program (College of Business) is open to Chicagoland entrepreneurs, and the Health Technology Incubator rents space to non-UIC startups, so a UIUC founder based in Chicago could use those as a member of the public. The Summer Venture Accelerator page said it would not run in Summer 2025. UIC OTM contact: otm@uic.edu.
